newsitem.title: USA: Noranda's Heath Steele zinc mine closed.
newsitem.headline: Noranda's Heath Steele zinc mine closed.

text.p: Canada's Noranda Inc said its Heath Steele zinc and lead mine in New Brunswick was still closed following an explosion which killed one miner and injured another late afternoon on Monday.
"Production-wise the mine is not expected to be closed for a lengthy period, but it's still very early to tell," said Ivan Miller, Noranda's vice president, commercial.

"The mine is closed at the moment because we are taking care to make sure we know exactly what caused it (the explosion), that there are no further safety issues," Miller said. "We will know more in another day, I am sure."
Heath Steele produces 100,000 tonnes a year of zinc concentrates, or 8,000 to 9,000 tonnes per month, and a small amount of lead concentrates, Miller said.
All the zinc concentrates from Heath Steele are shipped to third party customers. "At this point there will be a small delay, obviously. A small loss of production," Miller said.
The concentrate is shipped by vessels and the next departure was not due until the end of November. "There is no impact on that," Miller said.
Lead concentrate from Heath Steele is consumed by Noranda's own Belledune smelter.
This is the second disruption Noranda has suffered in its zinc and lead mining operations in the past few months.
In late August Noranda said production at its much bigger Brunswick mine was being cut because of seismic activity.
Miller said Tuesday that Brunswick was producing at the rate of 8,500 tonnes per day of ore at present, but the mine was on target to reach about 9,000 tonnes per day by early next year.
The estimated loss of zinc in 1996 at Brunswick was still 40,000 tonnes of contained metal, Miller added.
